title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because McNeil had not submitted to a regular trial; alternatively, if treated as a complaint, judicially out of order under BCO 43-2 for failure first to present it to Chesapeake Presbytery and because the 30-day period had expired. Complaints about later court actions while under censure are also barred until the censure is removed, except as to the highest censure.
first_summary: An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery's judicial commission process and censure. The SJC dismissed the appeal because he had not submitted to a regular trial and therefore could not appeal under BCO 42-2. If treated as a complaint, it was also out of order because he had not first brought it to the presbytery and the 30-day period had expired. The merits were not reached.
summary: An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery's judicial commission process and censure. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order—not decided on the merits—because he had not submitted to a regular trial, as BCO 42-2 requires. Treated as a complaint, it was also out of order: it had not first been presented to the presbytery, and the 30-day period had expired. The SJC further barred complaints about later court actions while he remained under censure, except as to the highest censure. The censure stood.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2010-03, McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery; SJC decision adopted by the full Standing Judicial Commission: lines 1-3, 79-87 (15 concurred, 1 disqualified, 6 absent).
evidence_notes.dispute: McNeil received censure of suspension from the sacraments after the CP Judicial Commission found strong presumption of guilt and he refused to enter a plea; CP approved the action, and McNeil appealed to the SJC: lines 17-33.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC held the appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because there was no regular trial; if construed as a complaint, it was judicially out of order under BCO 43-2 for not first going to CP and for untimeliness; post-censure complaints are barred until the censure is removed, except as to the highest censure: lines 37-41, 45-55, 60-69, 71-77.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The appeal was not decided on the merits; the underlying censure remained in effect. The roll call shows 15 concurred, 1 disqualified because he was a member of Chesapeake Presbytery, and 6 absent: lines 81-87.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision was supplied. The opinion cites BCO provisions and SJCM 20.9-20.10, but does not adopt another case's judgment: lines 68, 73-77.
